Sample Creative Direction for a Community Health Client

AI-Generated Imagery & Rise 360 Color Options • Sample

This sample demonstrates how a visual palette can bring consistency to a community health training series while remaining fresh, timeless, and flexible enough to scale across multiple modules. Each direction combines AI-generated documentary photography with a coordinated color system and Rise 360 interface mockups, allowing the color, typography, and imagery to be viewed together as learners would experience them. All three options share the same structural foundation while exploring a distinct set of visual accents.

Option A
Clinical Blue — Monochromatic
Structure #16193E
Interactive #0B6A8A
Accent #48AEE1
Tint #EDF4F7
Crisis Intervention and Safety Planning
Supporting individuals through safety planning and de-escalation techniques used in community-based settings.
Reflective Responses
Reflecting back what an individual has said confirms accurate hearing and surfaces insights that weren't visible in the original telling.
Practice Moment
Consider a recent interaction where frustration came up. What did you reflect back? What might you have missed?
Key Takeaway
Active listening requires deliberate attention to both the words and the emotions underneath them.
What would you do next?
The individual you're working with has expressed feelings of hopelessness during a home visit.
Review the safety plan together
Contact the crisis hotline immediately
Ask them to describe what they're feeling
‹
Step 1 of 4
›
Observe
Before responding, pause and take in the full picture. What is the individual saying? What are they not saying? What do you notice about their environment, body language, and energy?
Option B
Community-Based Warmth
Structure #16193E
Interactive #0B6A8A
Accent #D4940A
Tint #EDF4F7
Motivational Interviewing
Exploring motivational interviewing techniques that support individuals in identifying their own reasons for change.
The Spirit of MI
MI is built on partnership, not persuasion. The worker's role is to draw out the individual's own motivation rather than impose external reasons for change.
Open-Ended Questions
How might you reframe your questions to invite an individual to explore their own ambivalence about a treatment goal?
Key Takeaway
Resistance is information. When someone pushes back, they're telling you what matters to them.
Which response is most aligned with MI?
An individual says: "I don't see the point of taking my medication anymore."
"Tell me more about what's been going on."
"You need to keep taking it — it's in your plan."
"It sounds like something has changed."
‹
Step 2 of 4
›
Decide
Based on what you've observed, choose a response strategy. What approach fits this person, this moment, and this environment? There's no single right answer — the goal is intentional action.
Option C
Therapeutic Ground
Structure #16193E
Interactive #0B6A8A
Accent #477A5D
Tint #EDF4F7
Trauma-Informed Assessment in Practice
Understanding how trauma histories shape an individual's presentation and how to conduct assessments that prioritize safety and trust.
Trauma Responses
What looks like disengagement may be a trauma response. Workers learn to distinguish between clinical symptoms and adaptive survival behaviors.
Emotional Safety
What does safety look like where you provide services? How do you know when someone feels safe enough to engage?
Key Takeaway
Trauma-informed care is a lens, not a technique. Every interaction is an opportunity to reinforce safety.
What do you notice first?
During a home visit, an individual avoids eye contact and gives one-word answers. They agreed to the visit but seem withdrawn.
Slow down — this could be a trauma response
They're disengaged — try a different activity
"Is something making this hard today?"
‹
Step 3 of 4
›
Adjust
Pay attention to how the individual responds. If your approach isn't landing, shift. Flexibility is a clinical skill — staying rigid with a plan that isn't working serves the plan, not the person.

What's Consistent Across All Three

Deep blue structure — #16193E. Lesson openers, closers, section headers.

Teal-blue interaction — #0B6A8A. Every link, button, and interactive moment.

White canvas — clean reading surface. Photos carry all the warmth.

Cool tint — #EDF4F7 for gentle emphasis sections.

Plus Jakarta Sans — one font family for the entire series. Bold for headings, regular for body. Humanist warmth, strong readability, dyslexia-friendly letterforms.

Documentary photography — set in the homes, neighborhoods, and everyday spaces where community-based work happens.

All WCAG AA accessible — every text pairing passes accessibility standards.

WCAG AA Contrast Audit

Every color pairing checked against WCAG 2.1 AA requirements. Normal text needs 4.5:1, large text (18px+ or 14px+ bold) needs 3:1.
